address: Hoofdbureau van Politie, Elandsgracht 117, Amsterdam (Jordaan, corner of Marnixstraat)
notes: walls[0] (3DBAG panels 80, 26, 9): the long north-west wall on the street (panorama 2025-06-30, 2016-08-17) is dark brick with white steel-window ribbons on every storey and a glazed ground ribbon; ribbon-windows since 2026-10-13 (it was a punched bay grid, which the review sheet and a user photo showed wrong). The gated vehicle entrance and the round windows of its end pier are not modelled. The courtyard-side walls of the same wing (panel 26) are assumed the same (inferred).

walls[2] (panel 3, surface 4): the south-west wall on the Singelgracht (panorama 2021-01-25) is NOT brick: pinkish stone cladding with square yellow-framed windows in three rows of ~11, a yellow-framed top ribbon, a large yellow-framed glazed bay at ground and a stone sculpture group on a bracket at the left. Drawn by the builder from the measured rows (see the rework note).

walls[3] (surface 233 and the corner walls): the 45 m Marnixstraat front of the north wing is dark brick with four storeys of white steel-window ribbons over a ground storey (panoramas 2025-07-03 recording_2025-07-03_10-58-37_00361, 2020-08-31; user photo 2026-10-13). walls[4] (surface 190) is that wing's north end wall: blank in the kit, because the builder draws its wrapped ribbons, the Amsterdam arms relief with lions and banner, three figures on brackets, six round windows and the colonnade by hand (addEndWallRelief).
walls[5] (surfaces 171, 113): the low bridge wing on the Singelgracht (review-sheet panorama 2021) is two storeys of white steel-window ribbons over a brick base: ribbon-windows since 2026-10-13.

walls[9], [11], [12] (panels 48, 7, 13: the 157 deg south-east fronts): 1941 brick with sash windows and heavy white stone hoods and sills, brick chequer bands between the window rows (panorama 2025-07-03, 2021-09-09). The hoods are hand-modelled by the builder; the chequer bands and barred basement windows are not.

walls[7] (panel 19, surfaces 38 and 121): the Marnixstraat end block (panorama 2020-08-31, 2024-12-16): brick with a ribbon of two-light windows on the middle floors and a glazed ground floor with a stair and a flat canopy on one post. Drawn by the builder from measurements since the rework (see the rework note); the entrance and POLITIE are on the Marnixstraat front walls[3], not here.
Walls of groups [1], [6], [10], [13]-[15] are inferred from the eaves height and the neighbouring walls: no panorama reaches them; windows follow the default bay pitch.

walls[8] and walls[15] stand on raised ground in 3DBAG (16.9 m and 8.6 m): the fit counts storeys from the 3DBAG ground, so windows start at the first storey line above the raised ground. Surfaces with a sliver width (3DBAG strips under 0.5 m) are left out of the groups: they break the block kit's attachment gate.

Rework 2026-10-13 (lane hoofdbureau-rework): every photographed front is measured in scripts/landmarks/hoofdbureau-elandsgracht-facades.json (rectified panorama crops, metre grid) and the builder draws from those numbers. Groups that the photos show the kit cannot express are blank here and drawn by hoofdbureauHooks: walls[2] (the pink quay front w09: windows on the measured 1.85 m pitch, glazed bay, low and top ribbons, the void under the cantilever, the stone pair on its console), walls[4] (end wall w16: open ground storey on four columns, round windows, Krop figures, banner, arms), walls[7] (the Marnixstraat end block w15: ground hall behind a corner column, two-storey window block with the balcony, ledge, two-storey glazed top under a bowed roof slab, police sign), walls[16] (surface 10, w14: the tall brick end with four French windows on semicircular balconies), walls[17] (surfaces 44/174, w20: the glazed stair bay), walls[18] (surface 164, w23: the framed bay).

walls[3] (the 56 m Marnixstraat front w02) has four storeys, not five: a ground ribbon and three upper ribbons (2021 and 2024 crops). Its main entrance with the POLITIE word mark and police emblem is drawn by the builder at the measured s 34.3-38.3; from s 41.5 to the corner, and round the corner on w16 and w22, the ground storey is open on columns (the arcade at the Elandsgracht corner).

walls[11] (surfaces 41/8, the photographed 1941 wing w07): the ground storey has no windows, only barred basement windows at street level under the first-floor windows (2025 panorama); ground 'blank' since the rework, the builder draws the basement windows.
